backlog.title: Bug Fix — CI Coverage Gate Enforcement & Examples Type-Safety
backlog.description: Resolves the two defects surfaced by the end-to-end QA validation of plan 002_78ea74508dd8 (Phase P1: Type-Safety Completion & Coverage Gate). Issue 1 (Critical): the 90% coverage gate is configured in vitest.config.ts but never invoked by CI, violating PRD §1.3.7. Issue 2 (Minor, scope-corrected): `pnpm typecheck:examples` fails with 293 errors across ALL 9 example files (the PRD understated this as 12 errors in one file), and the check is not wired into CI. Both fixes are configuration/type-only — no new runtime dependencies, no product behavior changes. See plan/002_78ea74508dd8/bugfix/001_707393fb1b38/architecture/ for verified evidence.

milestones.title: Enforce the 90% coverage gate in CI (Issue 1 — Critical)
milestones.description: Make CI actually run the coverage gate so PRD §1.3.7's 'MUST maintain ≥ 90%… enforced by vitest coverage thresholds AND run in CI… the build fails if any metric drops below 90%' is satisfied in the only place enforcement matters. The vitest.config.ts thresholds block (added in P1.M2.T1.S5 of the original plan) is already correct and matches §1.3.7 verbatim; only the CI invocation is missing. This is a genuine one-line change.

tasks.title: Replace `pnpm test` with `pnpm test:coverage` in the CI verify job
tasks.description: The CI workflow runs `pnpm test` (= `vitest run`, no `--coverage`). Vitest only computes coverage and evaluates the thresholds block when coverage is enabled, so the 90% gate is completely inert in CI. Switch the test step to `pnpm test:coverage` (= `vitest run --coverage`) so the existing thresholds block fires and CI fails below 90%.

subtasks.title: Switch CI test step to the coverage-gated run
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/002_78ea74508dd8/bugfix/001_707393fb1b38/architecture/ci_coverage_gate.md. The vitest.config.ts `thresholds` block ({ statements: 90, branches: 90, functions: 90, lines: 90 }) is CORRECT and matches PRD §1.3.7 verbatim — do NOT touch it. The ONLY defect is that CI never invokes coverage. Coverage currently sits at 97.29%/95.56%/99.07%/97.29%, comfortably above 90%, so the first gated CI run will be green.
2. INPUT: Edit `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. The `verify` job has steps in this order: checkout → setup pnpm → setup node (cache: pnpm) → `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` → `pnpm lint` → `pnpm typecheck` → `- run: pnpm test` (the defect, ~line 38) → build core+react. The `pnpm test:coverage` script already exists in root package.json as `vitest run --coverage`.
3. LOGIC: Implement PRD §1.3.7 / Issue 1. Replace exactly the `- run: pnpm test` step with `- run: pnpm test:coverage`. Keep the step ordering and the subsequent build step intact. Do NOT add `pnpm test:coverage` to `.github/workflows/release.yml` (release.yml only builds + publishes via changesets and intentionally does not run tests). Do NOT duplicate threshold logic into CI — vitest.config.ts is the single source of truth. Do NOT add provider caching (optional hardening is out of scope; track separately). Validation (since CI YAML is not unit-testable in-repo): (a) confirm `pnpm test:coverage` exits 0 locally; (b) confirm vitest.config.ts `thresholds` is intact; (c) regression proof — temporarily set one threshold to 99 and confirm `pnpm test:coverage` now exits non-zero while `pnpm test` still exits 0, then REVERT the threshold. Optional: run `actionlint .github/workflows/ci.yml` if available to lint the YAML.
4. OUTPUT: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` with the verify job's test step running `pnpm test:coverage`, restoring the PRD §1.3.7 CI guarantee. No other files change.
5. DOCS: none — no user-facing/config/API surface change. README.md §Contributing/Testing already states coverage 'fails CI if any drops below 90%'; that claim was aspirational and becomes TRUE as a direct result of this change. The cross-cutting README narrative (CI now actually runs test:coverage + typecheck:examples) is handled by the final Mode-B documentation task P1.M2.T4.S1. Do not create a separate docs subtask here.

milestones.title: Restore example type-safety and gate it in CI (Issue 2 — Minor, scope-corrected)
milestones.description: Make `pnpm typecheck:examples` exit 0 and prevent regression by adding it to CI. NOTE: the PRD understated this — verified reality is 293 errors across ALL 9 example files (not 12 in one file). Root cause is uniform: every example imports the core framework-agnostic `InputConfig` (where `component: unknown`) instead of the React overlay `ReactInputConfig` (where `component: ComponentType<any>`). Fixing the type annotations resolves the bulk of errors; a residual sweep clears expression/operator widening. This milestone ends with a Mode-B documentation sync task. See plan/002_78ea74508dd8/bugfix/001_707393fb1b38/architecture/examples_typecheck.md for the per-file error counts and the fix patterns.

tasks.title: Migrate example type annotations from core InputConfig to the React overlay types
tasks.description: Replace core `InputConfig` / `FormFieldsConfig` annotations with the React overlay types `ReactInputConfig` / `ReactFormFieldsConfig` (and/or `defineInputs`) across all 9 example files, updating imports accordingly. This restores `ComponentType<any>` contextual typing on inline components and resolves the bulk of the 293 errors: TS2322 (61, component: unknown → ComponentType), TS2339 (175, property access on {} props), TS7031/TS7006 (30, implicit-any params), TS2739/TS2741 (5, FormFieldsConfig vs ReactFormFieldsConfig key mismatch).

subtasks.title: Migrate input & field-config type annotations to React overlay types across all 9 examples
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/002_78ea74508dd8/bugfix/001_707393fb1b38/architecture/examples_typecheck.md. ALL 9 files in examples/*.tsx import `type InputConfig` (core, `component: unknown`) and annotate `const inputs: Record<string, InputConfig>` — this is the root cause. Verified per-file error counts: 04-validation (57), 08-real-world-example (40), 02-input-types (34), 07-advanced-features (32), 05-field-dependencies (31), 09-string-vs-function (28), 03-conditions (26), 06-auto-save (24), 01-basic-form (21) = 293 total. The correct React overlay types are exported from `@formality-ui/react` (re-exported from packages/react/src/overlays.ts): `ReactInputConfig<TValue=unknown>` (component: ComponentType<any>, template?: ComponentType<InputTemplateProps>), `ReactFormFieldsConfig<V extends FieldValues = FieldValues>` (keys narrowed to Extract<keyof V, string>), `defineInputs<T extends Record<string, ReactInputConfig>>(inputs: T): T` (identity helper), `ReactFieldConfig<V>`.
2. INPUT: Source files: examples/01-basic-form.tsx, 02-input-types.tsx, 03-conditions.tsx, 04-validation.tsx, 05-field-dependencies.tsx, 06-auto-save.tsx, 07-advanced-features.tsx, 08-real-world-example.tsx, 09-string-vs-function.tsx. No dependency on other subtasks — these are self-contained type-only edits. The `@formality-ui/react` package build (packages/react/dist) is what examples resolve; confirm `ReactInputConfig`, `ReactFormFieldsConfig`, `defineInputs` are present in packages/react/src/index.ts (verified: lines ~93, ~96, ~108).
3. LOGIC: Implement PRD §1.3.7 / Issue 2 fix step 1. For each file: (a) change the `import { type InputConfig }` to `import { type ReactInputConfig }` (from `@formality-ui/react`); (b) change `Record<string, InputConfig>` → `Record<string, ReactInputConfig>`; (c) where a config object is annotated `FormFieldsConfig`, switch to `ReactFormFieldsConfig` (also import from `@formality-ui/react`) — this resolves TS2739 key-mismatch errors; (d) ALTERNATIVELY/ADDITIONALLY use `defineInputs({...})` for the inputs map where idiomatic (matches overlays.ts JSDoc and also enables `type InputType = keyof typeof inputs`). SPECIAL CASE examples/02-input-types.tsx declares individual inputs as `const textField: InputConfig = {...}` AND a generic one `const autocomplete: InputConfig<Option | null>` — migrate EACH to `ReactInputConfig` / `ReactInputConfig<Option | null>`. examples/07-advanced-features.tsx has a SECOND inputs map (`templateInputs`) — migrate both. These are TYPE-ONLY edits — do not change runtime behavior, JSX structure, or the demonstrated concepts. Validation: run `pnpm typecheck:examples` after migration; expect the error count to drop sharply (bulk of TS2322/TS2339/TS7031/TS7006/TS2739 resolved). Residual errors are handled by P1.M2.T2.S1.
4. OUTPUT: All 9 example files import and use the React overlay types; `pnpm typecheck:examples` error count reduced to only residual expression/operator/arg-count errors (TS2365/TS2362/TS2363/TS2554/TS2769). Hand the remaining error list to P1.M2.T2.S1.
5. MOCKING: None — examples compile against the already-built `@formality-ui/react` dist types; no runtime services involved.
6. DOCS: none — these are example-internal type edits with no change to the library's public API, exported types, or config surface. The shipped examples are user-facing docs in the broad sense, but no README/config doc is touched by per-file type-annotation swaps; the cross-cutting 'examples are now type-clean' narrative is handled by the final Mode-B task P1.M2.T4.S1.

tasks.title: Clear residual expression/operator widening & arg-count errors
tasks.description: After the type-annotation migration (P1.M2.T1.S1) clears the bulk of errors, sweep the residuals — arithmetic/comparison operators on widened `{}` operands (TS2365/TS2362/TS2363), wrong-arg-count call sites (TS2554), and overload mismatches (TS2769) — until `pnpm typecheck:examples` exits 0. Concentrated in examples/09-string-vs-function.tsx but sweep every file.

subtasks.title: Sweep residual widening/arg-count errors to reach `pnpm typecheck:examples` exit 0
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/002_78ea74508dd8/bugfix/001_707393fb1b38/architecture/examples_typecheck.md. After P1.M2.T1.S1, the remaining errors are expected to be: TS2365 (6, 'Operator >= cannot be applied to types {} and number'), TS2362/TS2363 (8, arithmetic on {} operands), TS2554 (7, wrong number of arguments), TS2769 (1, toFixed/toString overload on {}). These are concentrated in examples/09-string-vs-function.tsx string-expression DSL demos (e.g. `age >= 21`, `quantity * unitPrice`) where the example deliberately shows string expressions, but the TS errors are on the CALLBACK-FUNCTION variants where `fields.age?.value` widens to `{}`. NOTE: depending on how P1.M2.T1.S1 types things, some of these may already be resolved — re-run `pnpm typecheck:examples` and fix whatever remains.
2. INPUT: The 9 example files post-migration (dependency P1.M2.T1.S1). The current residual error list from `pnpm typecheck:examples`.
3. LOGIC: Implement PRD §1.3.7 / Issue 2 fix step 2. Iterate: run `pnpm typecheck:examples`, read each remaining error, fix it. Patterns: (a) for callback-function selectProps/selectWhen/selectSet/selectDefaultFieldProps where operands widen, provide a `number` fallback + annotation, e.g. `const age = fields.age?.value ?? 0;` then `if (age >= 21 ...)` — ensure the `?? 0` yields `number` (may need `Number(...)` cast or explicit `: number`); (b) for arg-count errors (TS2554), align the call signature with the documented Formality callback shape `({ fields }: FormState) => ...`; (c) for overload mismatches (TS2769), cast the operand to `number` before calling. These are TYPE-SAFETY edits to shipped example docs — preserve the demonstrated concept (string vs function comparison) exactly; only make the TypeScript happy. Do NOT introduce `@ts-ignore`/`@ts-expect-error` to mask errors (that defeats the purpose of type-clean examples).
4. OUTPUT: `pnpm typecheck:examples` exits 0 with zero errors across all 9 example files. This is the gate for P1.M2.T3.S1 (which adds the check to CI) and the final docs task.
5. MOCKING: None.
6. DOCS: none — example-internal type edits, no library public API/config surface change. Cross-cutting 'examples are type-clean' narrative → final Mode-B task P1.M2.T4.S1.

subtasks.title: Add `pnpm typecheck:examples` step to the CI verify job
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/002_78ea74508dd8/bugfix/001_707393fb1b38/architecture/external_deps.md. The `typecheck:examples` script (`tsc -p examples/tsconfig.json --noEmit`) is NOT currently a CI step. examples/tsconfig.json is composite + jsx:react-jsx, referencing packages/core + packages/react, and is NOT part of the main `tsc --build` graph (script `typecheck`), so its errors are invisible to CI. PRD §1.3.7 excludes examples from the COVERAGE gate but examples are still shipped user-facing documentation and should compile. PRD Issue 2 explicitly recommends wiring this into CI.
2. INPUT: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (already modified by P1.M1.T1.S1 so the test step now runs `pnpm test:coverage`). The examples must already be clean (dependency P1.M2.T2.S1 — `pnpm typecheck:examples` exits 0). The script `typecheck:examples` already exists in root package.json.
3. LOGIC: Implement PRD Issue 2 fix step 3. Add a new step to the `verify` job, placed immediately after the existing `pnpm typecheck` step and before (or after) the test step — recommended placement: right after `pnpm typecheck` to keep type-checking steps grouped: `- run: pnpm typecheck`. Add `- run: pnpm typecheck:examples`. Keep it BLOCKING (exit non-zero on error) — the examples are now clean, so blocking is the correct choice per PRD Issue 2's 'wire the check into CI accordingly'. Do NOT add it to release.yml. Validation: confirm `pnpm typecheck:examples` exits 0 locally before/after the edit; optionally `actionlint` the YAML.
4. OUTPUT: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` verify job now runs `typecheck:examples`; example type regressions fail CI.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update README.md §Scripts table to add a row for `pnpm typecheck:examples` (currently the table lists build/test/test:coverage/typecheck/lint only). The CI step makes this script a first-class gate, so documenting it rides WITH this work. Add the row near the `typecheck` row: `| pnpm typecheck:examples | Type-check the examples directory |` (backticks optional in the table cell). This is the per-file doc the change directly touches. The broader CI-narrative update (README §Contributing/Testing describing what CI runs) is the final Mode-B task P1.M2.T4.S1 — do not duplicate it here.
